1	# Guava: Google Core Libraries for Java
2	
3	[![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/google/guava)](https://github.com/google/guava/releases/latest)
4	[![CI](https://github.com/google/guava/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/google/guava/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
5	[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/7197/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/7197)
6	
7	
8	
9	Guava is a set of core Java libraries from Google that includes new collection
10	types (such as multimap and multiset), immutable collections, a graph library,
11	and utilities for concurrency, I/O, hashing, primitives, strings, and more! It
12	is widely used on most Java projects within Google, and widely used by many
13	other companies as well.
14	
15	
16	
17	Guava comes in two flavors:
18	
19	*   The JRE flavor requires JDK 1.8 or higher.
20	*   If you need support for Android, use
21	    [the Android flavor](https://github.com/google/guava/wiki/Android). You can
22	    find the Android Guava source in the [`android` directory].
23	
24	[`android` directory]: https://github.com/google/guava/tree/master/android
25	
26	## Adding Guava to your build
27	
28	Guava's Maven group ID is `com.google.guava`, and its artifact ID is `guava`.
29	Guava provides two different "flavors": one for use on a (Java 8+) JRE and one
30	for use on Android or by any library that wants to be compatible with Android.
31	These flavors are specified in the Maven version field as either `33.6.0-jre` or
32	`33.6.0-android`. For more about depending on Guava, see
33	[using Guava in your build].
34	
35	To add a dependency on Guava using Maven, use the following:
36	
37	```xml
38	<dependency>
39	  <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
40	  <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
41	  <version>33.6.0-jre</version>
42	  <!-- or, for Android: -->
43	  <version>33.6.0-android</version>
44	</dependency>
45	```
46	
47	To add a dependency using Gradle:
48	
49	```gradle
50	dependencies {
51	  // Pick one:
52	
53	  // 1. Use Guava in your implementation only:
54	  implementation("com.google.guava:guava:33.6.0-jre")
55	
56	  // 2. Use Guava types in your public API:
57	  api("com.google.guava:guava:33.6.0-jre")
58	
59	  // 3. Android - Use Guava in your implementation only:
60	  implementation("com.google.guava:guava:33.6.0-android")
61	
62	  // 4. Android - Use Guava types in your public API:
63	  api("com.google.guava:guava:33.6.0-android")
64	}
65	```
66	
67	For more information on when to use `api` and when to use `implementation`,
68	consult the
69	[Gradle documentation on API and implementation separation](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/java_library_plugin.html#sec:java_library_separation).
70	
71	## Snapshots and Documentation
72	
73	Snapshots of Guava built from the `master` branch are available through Maven
74	using version `999.0.0-HEAD-jre-SNAPSHOT`, or `999.0.0-HEAD-android-SNAPSHOT`
75	for the Android flavor.
76	
77	[Snapshot API Javadoc][guava-snapshot-api-docs] as well as
78	[Snapshot API Diffs][guava-snapshot-api-diffs] are also available.
79	
80	Another easy way to get to the Javadoc is to open
81	[guava.dev/api](https://guava.dev/api). You can also jump right to a specific
82	class by appending the class name to guava.dev. For example,
83	[guava.dev/ImmutableList](https://guava.dev/ImmutableList)!
84	
85	## Learn about Guava
86	
87	-   Our users' guide, [Guava Explained]
88	-   [A nice collection](https://www.tfnico.com/presentations/google-guava) of
89	    other helpful links
90	
91	## Links
92	
93	-   [GitHub project](https://github.com/google/guava)
94	-   [Issue tracker: Report a defect or feature request](https://github.com/google/guava/issues/new)
95	-   [StackOverflow: Ask "how-to" and "why-didn't-it-work" questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=guava+java)
96	-   [guava-announce: Announcements of releases and upcoming significant changes](https://groups.google.com/group/guava-announce)
97	-   [guava-discuss: For open-ended questions and discussion](https://groups.google.com/group/guava-discuss)
98	
99	## IMPORTANT WARNINGS
100	
101	1.  APIs marked with the `@Beta` annotation at the class or method level are
102	    subject to change. They can be modified in any way, or even removed, at any
103	    time. If your code is a library itself (i.e., it is used on the CLASSPATH of
104	    users outside your own control), you should not use beta APIs unless you
105	    [repackage] them. **If your code is a library, we strongly recommend using
106	    the [Guava Beta Checker] to ensure that you do not use any `@Beta` APIs!**
107	
108	2.  APIs without `@Beta` will remain binary-compatible for the indefinite
109	    future. (Previously, we sometimes removed such APIs after a deprecation
110	    period. The last release to remove non-`@Beta` APIs was Guava 21.0.) Even
111	    `@Deprecated` APIs will remain (again, unless they are `@Beta`). We have no
112	    plans to start removing things again, but officially, we're leaving our
113	    options open in case of surprises (like, say, a serious security problem).
114	
115	3.  Guava has one dependency that is needed for linkage at runtime:
116	    `com.google.guava:failureaccess:1.0.3`. It also has
117	    [some annotation-only dependencies][guava-deps], which we discuss in more
118	    detail at that link.
119	
120	4.  Serialized forms of ALL objects are subject to change unless noted
121	    otherwise. Do not persist these and assume they can be read by a future
122	    version of the library.
123	
124	5.  Our classes are not designed to protect against a malicious caller. You
125	    should not use them for communication between trusted and untrusted code.
126	
127	6.  For the mainline flavor, we test the libraries using a range of OpenJDK
128	    versions on Linux and Windows. Some features, especially in
129	    `com.google.common.io`, may not work correctly in non-Linux environments.
130	    For the Android flavor, our unit tests also run on API level 23
131	    (Marshmallow).
132

134	[guava-snapshot-api-diffs]: https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot-jre/api/diffs/

## Comprehensive Codebase Overview: Google Guava

**Project Type:** Java utility library (core Google libraries)

**Build System:** Maven (version 999.0.0-HEAD-jre-SNAPSHOT, targeting JDK 1.8+)

**License:** Apache 2.0

### Top-Level Directory Structure

├── guava-bom/              # Bill of Materials POM
├── android/                # Android-specific flavor
├── futures/                # Future-related utilities (ListenableFuture, etc.)
├── util/                   # Utility scripts
├── integration-tests/      # Integration test suite
├── pom.xml                 # Parent Maven configuration

├── proguard/               # ProGuard configuration for obfuscation
├── CONTRIBUTING.md

```

### Main Source Packages (guava/src/com/google/common/)

The core library is organized into functional modules:

- **collect/** - Advanced collections (Multimap, Multiset, ImmutableList/Set/Map, Range, etc.)
- **cache/** - Caching utilities with LoadingCache
- **base/** - Core utilities (Preconditions, Strings, Charsets, Optional, etc.)
- **util/** - Utility classes including concurrent utilities
- **io/** - I/O utilities (Files, ByteStreams, CharStreams, etc.)
- **hash/** - Hashing functions and BloomFilter
- **net/** - Network utilities (URL encoding, InternetDomainName, etc.)
- **math/** - Mathematical utilities (BigDecimal/Integer operations)
- **primitives/** - Primitive array utilities (Ints, Longs, Bytes, etc.)
- **reflect/** - Reflection utilities (TypeToken, Invokable)
- **escape/** - HTML, JSON, XML escaping utilities
- **eventbus/** - Event publish/subscribe mechanism
- **graph/** - Graph data structures
- **html/** - HTML utilities
- **xml/** - XML utilities
- **annotations/** - Custom annotations (@Beta, @VisibleForTesting)

### Build Configuration

The multi-module Maven project builds:
1. **guava** - Core JRE library
2. **guava-testlib** - Test helper library for others to use
3. **guava-tests** - Comprehensive test suite
4. **guava-gwt** - GWT-compatible version
5. **guava-bom** - Dependency bill of materials
6. **android/** - Android flavor (separate packaging)
